city_metadata.title: SETTINGS SERVICE
city_metadata.subtitle: Spec ↔ code · Typed configuration and feature flags with tenant-scoped inheritance and validate-then-set writes.
city_metadata.scale_axis_description: South to north: requirements → design → features → code; roads are traceability links.

districts.name: 1 · REQUIREMENTS
districts.description: Functional requirements from the PRD (29); non-functional ones (9) stand as goals.

districts.name: 3 · FEATURES
districts.scale_label: What gets built, and in what order
districts.description: The decomposition into 11 features: each covers requirements and components and is specified as flows, algorithms and definitions of done.

districts.name: 4 · CODE
districts.description: 234 Rust files in 21 modules; @cpt markers tie code blocks to the spec items they implement.

spires.title: Category and Setting Lifecycle
spires.abstract: The system MUST let a platform administrator create a named, flat, single-level category with a unique name and description; creating a category with a duplicate name MUST be rejected with a clear error. The system MUST reject removal of a category while one or more settings, active or retired, remain filed under it…

spires.title: Purge of a Retired Setting

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: The system MUST let a platform administrator permanently remove (purge) a setting that is retired. The system MUST refuse to purge an active setting — it is retired first — and MUST refuse to purge a module-contributed setting, whose lifecycle its owning gear governs (cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-contributed-lifecycle…

spires.title: GTS Type Validation, Trait Discovery & Secret Protection
spires.abstract: The system MUST validate every setting value (override or default) against its declared GTS type at creation or change time and MUST reject invalid values with a clear, field-level error; format keywords (e.g. uri, ipv4/ipv6) and trait-driven rules (e.g. cron dialect, regex-compiles) MUST be asserted, not treated as…

spires.title: File-Valued Settings
spires.abstract: Some configuration is a file rather than a scalar or a small structure — a tenant's branding logo, a Terms-of-Service document, SAML IdP metadata for a tenant's SSO, a custom CA bundle for outbound webhooks. The system MUST support a setting whose value is a file held by reference: the stored value identifies a file…

spires.title: Mode-Filtered Reads
spires.abstract: The system MUST tag every setting and category as Standard or Advanced. When a client reads categories or settings for Standard mode, Advanced-only settings and categories MUST be excluded; the user's mode preference MUST persist per user, not per session. When a category has hidden Advanced-only settings, reads MUST…

spires.title: Cross-Field Search
spires.abstract: The system MUST let an administrator search settings by key, display name, description, value, or category name and MUST return matches as a flat list with category breadcrumbs and an indication of which field matched. Search MUST respect the same scope, mode, and tenant-visibility filters as browsing.

spires.title: Revert to Ancestor or Schema Default

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: The system MUST maintain an independent Schema Default per setting that is never destroyed by setting an override. When an administrator reverts a tenant-scope override of a cascading setting, the system MUST clear the local override, fall the effective value back to the nearest ancestor's override (or the platform…

spires.title: Setting a Value
spires.abstract: A value operation on a setting — set, revert, remove-value, or clone (at platform or any tenant scope) — MUST take effect when the caller sets it. The service MUST NOT keep the change in a pending state first, and there MUST NOT be a separate step that activates it later. A client that lets an administrator collect…

spires.title: Validate Before Setting; Step-Up on Set
spires.abstract: The system MUST let a caller ask what a value would do before setting it. This check MUST report whether the value is valid, the current effective value and where it comes from, and which descendant scopes the change would affect, in pages rather than all at once. It MUST change nothing, MUST give the same answer…

spires.title: A Value Activates via Live-Read; Consumers Self-React

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: Activating a change MUST NOT require the Settings Service to reload or restart any consumer: the new value becomes effective and each consumer reads it on next read (live-read / pull) via the settings SDK, with cache invalidation. The Settings Service MUST NOT declare or resolve a per-setting "effect"; live-read is…

spires.title: Replica Coherence After a Set
spires.abstract: The Settings Service runs as multiple replicas and a set is handled by one of them; the other replicas hold their own caches of the same effective values. After a value is set, every replica MUST converge on it — for the target scope and, for a cascading setting, for every descendant scope whose effective value the…

spires.title: Consumer Activation: Notify, Confirm, and Account
spires.abstract: A consuming gear MUST be able to register interest in the specific settings it depends on, and MUST then receive a change notification limited to those settings — never the rest of a set's contents, and never a setting it is not entitled to read. A notification MUST carry identifiers only and no setting value, so the…

spires.title: Dependency Group and Cross-Setting Constraint Declaration

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: The system MUST let a declaration author declare a Dependency Group — a named set of interdependent settings with an associated cross-setting constraint over their combined values — so that the all-or-nothing set and resulting-configuration validation required by cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-live-read-activation have an…

spires.title: Setting Scope Class Governs Cascade/Override Behaviour
spires.abstract: Every setting MUST declare a Scope Class (global | cascading | local), and cascade/override behaviour MUST be derived deterministically from it: global MUST NOT be overridable by any tenant nor inherited by tenants; cascading MUST inherit down the tenant scope hierarchy with overrides at permitted scopes; local MUST…

spires.title: Tenant Override of a Cascading Value
spires.abstract: Given a cascading setting with a platform-level value, when a value is set at a target tenant, it MUST override the inherited value there and for non-overriding descendants. The target MUST be inside the caller's subtree. A tenant caller may write only when the caller's own effective access to the setting is…

spires.title: Cascading Inheritance with Source Trace and Impact Warning
spires.abstract: For a cascading setting at a tenant scope, the system MUST resolve the effective value by walking up the tenant scope hierarchy — against the locally cached hierarchy snapshot on the warm read path, refreshed from tenant-resolver within a bounded freshness window (§6.1) — to the first override, else the platform…

spires.title: Subject-Scoped Values (Model-Level Identity)

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: A setting value MUST be identified by (declaration, scope) where scope is platform, tenant, or either of those qualified by a subject — (scope, subject_type, subject_id). A subject MUST NOT be required to belong to a tenant: a subject may exist at platform scope. subject_type MUST be a GTS-registered type and…

spires.title: Hierarchy Barriers: Standalone Tenants Are Opaque Upward

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: A tenant marked standalone (isolated / unmanaged, as modeled by tenant-resolver) MUST remain an ordinary inheritance target: a cascading setting MUST resolve into it from its parent chain exactly as into any other tenant, with no marking, exemption or per-declaration opt-in required. What standalone changes is the…

spires.title: Authentication and Access-Level Gating

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: Any Settings operation MUST require a valid authenticated session/token (via authn-resolver) and MUST be gated by an authorization decision via authz-resolver: view-level access permits read, owner/admin-level access permits mutate. An interactive write to a declaration that requires elevated confirmation (§5.7), and…

spires.title: Audited Mutations and Secret Reveals

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: Any mutating operation (create/set/revert/remove-value/clone, and a declaration's retire/reactivate/purge) MUST write an audit record with actor, target (category + key + scope), pre/post values (secrets masked), timestamp, outcome, and a request identifier; audit history MUST be queryable globally and per (setting…

spires.title: Per-Setting Access

metrics.maturity: In a planned feature, not yet done

spires.abstract: A right to read or change setting values covers every setting the caller can otherwise see, so "this role manages the billing settings, that one the infrastructure settings" cannot be expressed, and a gear authorized to write its own settings would be authorized to write everyone's.

spires.title: Feature/Licence Gating
spires.abstract: Given settings or categories whose visibility is restricted by a licence/feature flag (via license-resolver), when read, search, or list operations run, gated settings MUST be excluded for callers without the entitlement, enforced server-side consistently across all administrative read paths (UI/API browse, search…

spires.title: Elevated Confirmation, and Writes by Services
spires.abstract: A setting Declaration MUST carry a flag stating whether changing its value requires elevated confirmation. It MUST default to required, so a declaration that says nothing is protected, and clearing it MUST be a deliberate act on a setting whose value is machine-managed rather than a human decision.

spires.title: Anonymous-Exposable Values
spires.abstract: A setting Declaration MUST be markable anonymous-exposable, defaulting to not exposable. Marking it MUST be rejected when the setting's data classification is secret or pii, and un-marking MUST always be allowed. Marking and un-marking MUST be platform-administrator actions and MUST be audited, and the full set of…

spires.title: Gears Contribute Declarations; Admins Change Values
spires.abstract: When a gear that owns configuration is installed or upgraded, it MUST be able to contribute its Setting Declarations (namespaced key, GTS type, default, metadata including an optional display name, Scope Class) to the Settings Service, and administrators MUST be able to change the contributed settings' values (subject…

spires.title: Contributed-Declaration Register/Retire Lifecycle
spires.abstract: When a gear registers, upgrades, or retires a declaration, the Settings Service MUST reconcile the declaration set (add / update descriptive metadata / mark-retired), preserving administrator-set values across compatible upgrades. A gear upgrade MUST NOT change a contributed declaration's behavior-affecting fields…

spires.title: Bulk Effective-Value Retrieval
spires.abstract: The system MUST support retrieval of effective values in bulk — by key set and by category — as a single operation, with per-key outcomes (never all-or-nothing), on every read surface, subject to the same visibility, scope, and secret-masking rules as single reads. The administrative settings list — the bulk read an…

spires.title: Domain Affinity Filtering
spires.abstract: The system MUST support an optional Domain Affinity per setting (not every setting carries one); the hub MUST filter categories by the administrator's current domain. Cross-domain settings MUST be hidden by default (not read-only); a platform administrator MUST be able to switch to an "All domains" view. Domain…

spires.title: Component: Change Set Publisher
spires.abstract: Runs inside the Settings Service; invoked by the change set commit (DESIGN.md §4.2 *Value Writer*) after all values are written.

spires.title: Component: Event Broker Client
spires.abstract: Transport abstraction for sending and receiving notifications.

spires.title: Component: Subscription Manager
spires.abstract: Dependencies: Notification State (PostgreSQL). Subscription is self-contained: a consumer registers explicitly (register_subscription / SDK subscribe). There is no dependency on the Settings Service Contribution path and no auto-subscribe — contribution and subscription are fully independent.

spires.title: Component: Consumer Activation SDK
spires.abstract: The consumer-facing contract. Subscribes to specific setting keys, receives filtered change_notification bundles, re-reads the changed settings, and emits back-responses.

spires.title: Component: Change Set Outcome Tracker
spires.abstract: Tracks and exposes bundle state based on consumer responses. Runs in the Settings Service.

spires.title: Component: Cache Invalidation Broadcast
spires.abstract: Dependencies: Event Broker Client, Settings Service effective-value cache (DESIGN.md §4.2 *Cache & Invalidation* of that design).

spires.title: Component: Category Management
spires.abstract: Dependencies: PostgreSQL, AuthZResolverClient (with PolicyEnforcer built over it), LicenseResolverApi (License Resolver — feature/licence entitlement), Audit Emitter

spires.title: Component: Declaration Management
spires.abstract: Manages admin-authored declarations and serves reads for both authored and contributed declarations. Contributed declarations are written only via the Reconciler (§4.2 *Contribution Reconciler*).

spires.title: Component: Module Contribution Reconciler
spires.abstract: Realizes Module-Contributed Settings (cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-module-contributed-declarations, cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-contributed-lifecycle): gears register Setting Declarations on install/upgrade, and administrators change values. A gear that must write a value does so in the separate role of an authorized…

spires.title: Component: Type Validator (GTS + traits)
spires.abstract: Dependencies: TypesRegistryClient (GTS Schema Registry, in-process via ClientHub)

spires.title: Component: Value Resolver
spires.abstract: Resolves the effective value with source trace; the hot read path (cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-cascading-inheritance, cpt-cf-settings-service-nfr-performance-read-cache).

spires.title: Component: Tenant Access
spires.abstract: Stores tenant restrictions and resolves effective access (cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-tenant-scope-enforcement).

spires.title: Component: Value Writer
spires.abstract: Validates and stores value changes (cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-set-value, cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-validate-before-set, cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-live-read-activation, cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-tenant-overrides, cpt-cf-settings-service-nfr-reliability-validated-set).

spires.title: Component: Secret Manager
spires.abstract: Handles secret-trait values, backed by the platform Credential Store (the credstore backend, the credstore gear; gear dependency credstore). Plaintext never enters the settings DB, cache, search index, or audit trail — the settings row holds only an opaque secret_ref. create_declaration (§4.2 *Declaration Management*)…

spires.title: Component: Search
spires.abstract: Dependencies: PostgreSQL, AuthZResolverClient (with PolicyEnforcer built over it), LicenseResolverApi (License Resolver — feature/licence entitlement)

spires.title: Component: Cache & Invalidation
spires.abstract: Dependencies: in-memory store (local to the service instance), Event Broker

spires.title: Component: Actor Name Resolver
spires.abstract: Puts a display name beside the actor of each history record (cpt-cf-settings-service-fr-audit-mutations, cpt-cf-settings-service-actor-compliance-reviewer). It is a read-side helper of the history endpoint (§4.3). It writes nothing: mutation responses carry no actor name, and the audit record is unchanged. The display…

spires.title: Component: Audit Emitter
spires.abstract: Unlike RBAC v1, audit is a show-stopper here and is always active.

spires.abstract: Establish the settings-service-sdk crate and the gear scaffold every later feature builds on: domain models and the SettingKey value object, the Settings Reader and Contribution client traits, the error taxonomy and its RFC-9457 Problem mapping, PostgreSQL persistence with migration tooling, REST and OData…

spires.title: Category Management

metrics.acceleration: 16 of 16 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Provide the flat category taxonomy every setting declaration is filed under, with globally unique key and name, optional administrative-domain binding, display ordering, and no-orphan deletion. The category key is load-bearing beyond grouping: it becomes the <category> token of every setting key declared under it —…

spires.title: Setting Declarations and Scope Class

metrics.acceleration: 23 of 26 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Introduce the setting declaration as an entity distinct from its value, keyed by a GTS type identifier gts.cf.core.settings.setting_type.v1~<vendor>.settings.<category>.<name>.v1~ registered under the Settings gear's abstract base (ADR-002), and give each declaration a first-class scope class from which cascade and…

spires.title: Typed Value Validation

metrics.acceleration: 15 of 15 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Validate every setting value against the GTS value type its declaration names by value_type_id, as hard checks rather than advisory ones, and expose the resolved trait set that both drives client rendering and determines whether a setting is secret-backed. The service consumes GTS types; it never authors them.

spires.title: Effective Value Resolution, Defaults and Cache

metrics.acceleration: 23 of 23 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Resolve the effective value of a setting by dispatching on its scope class, returning a source trace alongside the value, and serve that hot path from a local in-process cache. This is the feature that makes the service useful to consumers, and it is the dependency almost every later feature waits on.

spires.title: Audit Store and History

metrics.acceleration: 12 of 12 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Replace the tracing stand-in behind the Audit Emitter with the R1 sink the design specifies: an append-only audit_records table written inside the mutation's own transaction through AuditSink::append(txn, scope, record), and the per-(setting, scope) history read served from it. Audit is a show-stopper here — a…

spires.title: Tenant Access Restrictions

metrics.acceleration: 15 of 15 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Let an ancestor's administrator narrow what one descendant may do with one setting — read_only or hidden, recorded sparsely, absence meaning overridable — and make the resulting effective access the single answer every read and write consults. Access is narrowing-only along the root-to-self chain, the platform has no…

spires.title: Validate and Set Values

metrics.acceleration: 22 of 22 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Deliver the write path: a read-only check of what a value would do, and set, revert, remove and clone operations that validate inline, refuse a stale write, take effect when the caller sets them, and are audited in the same transaction. This is where the StepUpVerifier port acquires its default binding over the…

spires.title: Secret Values

metrics.acceleration: 14 of 14 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Hold secret-trait values in the platform Credential Store and nowhere else: the settings row carries only an opaque secret_ref, every administrative read shows a mask, and the sole plaintext path is machine-only through the Settings Reader, authorized per setting and audited per resolution. A lost secret is re-set…

spires.title: Module-Contributed Declarations

metrics.acceleration: 14 of 14 spec items marked in code

spires.abstract: Let a gear register its own setting declarations from its init on every boot, idempotently, and retire them when it stops shipping them — the module supplying the derived half of each key and its value_type_id, the reconciler extracting the category from the derived half's third segment and creating it if absent, and…

metrics.acceleration: 8 of 8 spec items marked in code

tour.title: What it must do
tour.text: 29 functional requirements in the PRD: 12 checked off, 9 covered by a planned feature, 8 left for a later release (drawn as ghosts). Non-functional requirements stand as goals.
tour.look: Solid buildings are done; ghosts have no feature yet

tour.title: How it is shaped
tour.text: 18 design components. Each road up to the features says which feature builds it.
tour.look: Components and the roads to the features that build them

tour.title: Features: the contract between spec and code
tour.text: The decomposition splits the work into 11 features. Each is specified as flows, algorithms and definitions of done — 179 spec items in all — and the plaza counts how many of them the code marks.
tour.look: Feature towers (height = spec items) and the coverage plaza

tour.title: Where it lives
tour.text: 77,027 lines in 234 files. 173 of 179 spec items carry a @cpt marker in the code, so every road from a feature to a module is exact, not guessed.
tour.look: Module height = lines of code; roads = @cpt markers

tour.title: Where the trace breaks
tour.text: 6 spec items have no marker in the code, and some code has no marker at all. The map draws each gap where it acts.
